sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:72
items.html:
It explains: The matter of the refinement of the screen. And an explanation of the exit of the five levels, KHB, ZA, and Malchut, one below the other, by reason of the refinement of the screen.

The power of restraint in the screen, and the measure of coarseness in Malchut, are equal.
And in order to understand this refinement of the screen, we must preface two premises: The first is that the power of restraint in the screen is equal to the measure of coarseness, which is the yearning that is in phase four, like two pans of a scale. And the reason is simple: if the yearning to receive is great, one must exert great power to restrain oneself from receiving, and if the yearning is small, one need not exert oneself much to restrain from receiving. Hence the power of restraint in the screen is equal to the measure of coarseness in phase four, whether less or more.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:73
items.html:
The surrounding light's way is to refine the screen.
The second premise is that the nature of that surrounding light, which does not clothe in the emanated being, is to refine the coarseness in phase four, little by little, in the order of the four phases, until it refines all the coarseness in it entirely — beginning by refining it from phase four to phase three, then to phase two, then to phase one, and then it becomes completely refined through it, without any coarseness at all.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:74
items.html:
Because it wishes to clothe and the screen restrains it.
And the reason for this is that the surrounding light means that upper light which cannot clothe in the emanated being because the screen restrains it from expanding beyond the measure of its level, so it remains outside the Partzuf and surrounds it, meaning it shines on it from a distance. And since the surrounding light wishes to shine also in the internality of the Partzuf, in its manner in Ein Sof, which shone also in phase four, it therefore strikes the screen and refines it, meaning it nullifies the coarseness and hardness in it so it may be able to clothe.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:75
items.html:
First the screen grows stronger, and then the light grows stronger.
At first the screen grows stronger and pushes it backward, and then the light grows stronger and refines the screen. But it nullifies only that measure of coarseness on which the coupling by striking occurred. If the coupling by striking was in phase four, it nullifies the coarseness of phase four, which restrains it from clothing in the Partzuf, and leaves the coarseness of phase three, with which it has no business. And if the coupling by striking was in the coarseness of phase three, it nullifies only the coarseness of phase three, and leaves the coarseness of phase two, and so on (as written in Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Part 4, Inner Light, Chapter 1).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:76
items.html:
Phase four is not absent, even though it was refined into phase three.
And you already know that in every renewal of form that occurs spiritually, the previous form is not absent because of it, since there is no absence at all in the spiritual, but rather there is here an addition of form. Accordingly you will understand that this phase four, once refined into its phase three, is considered to have exited from this emanated being into the level of a new emanated being, added onto the first emanated being, in which the phase four is not phase four of phase four, but phase three of phase four. However, in the first emanated being, no change whatsoever occurred because of this refinement.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:77
items.html:
As soon as it is refined into phase three, the upper light couples with it, since it does not cease shining.
And it was explained above that the upper light does not cease shining to the lower ones even for a moment, and the matter of its expansion into the emanated being depends only on the preparation of its vessel, meaning according to the values of the will to receive in the emanated being, and whenever the emanated being awakens and yearns after the upper light, it attains it at once, in the measure of its will, as written above (Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, item 63, Sub Header, “And in that”). Therefore, once phase four was refined into its phase three, and exited as a new emanated being in its own right, it drew to itself the upper light, and then ten new Sefirot of the upper light went out in it from above downward, and also ten new Sefirot of reflected light from below upward, exactly in the manner of the expansion of the first emanated being. However there is a great distinction between them, in the measure of the level, for the new emanated being lacks the level of Keter and has only the level of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:78
items.html:
The reason why phase three lacks Keter.
And the reason for the lack of the level of Keter in this second emanated being is that it has no coarseness of phase four of phase four, which, in the aspect of the reflected light, is the Keter of phase four; therefore the screen returned the upper light only from Hochma downward, that is, the measure that was fit to come in phase three of phase four. This is unlike the phase of Keter of phase four, which had no expansion even if the screen had not restrained it, since the vessel that drew the upper light, from its very beginning, drew no more than Hochma downward; hence the screen did not return the light of Keter backward, but only from the light of Hochma downward, and so the light of Keter is lacking from this reflected light. And since the light of Keter is not there in the reflected light, the light of Keter of the upper light is not there either, since no light can clothe in the emanated being without the reflected light to clothe it, which is the aspect of its vessel of reception, as above (Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, item 21, Sub Header, “Now”). Hence it has only the level of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:79
items.html:
Every drawing is through phase four, and therefore it needs a screen so the light will not expand to phase four.
And this is the rule: every drawing of light must be only in phase four of the emanated being, even though there is no intention to draw light there. And the reason is that the coarseness that is above phase four is not fit for drawing, as above (Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, Chapter 5, item 56, Sub Header, “And a thing”), and even phase one of phase four is more fit for drawing than the true third phase, which is above it, meaning which is refined, of all phase four completely. Therefore, once all the coarseness of phase four has been exhausted, there is no longer anyone there to draw light from Ein Sof, and the light there ceases entirely. And since the drawing must be with phase four, and at the same time it must guard itself so that the light will not expand into its phase, on account of the restriction made on phase four, it therefore instituted within itself the screen that guards this matter: for at the time the light expands and reaches phase four, the screen awakens, and returns this portion of the light backward to its root, and that portion returned backward is not lost, but becomes the aspect of reflected light, meaning that from it comes the aspect of the vessel of reception for the upper light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:80
items.html:
Regarding the drawing of the light, phase four and the screen are as one.
Thus phase four and the screen upon it are one thing, regarding the drawing of light from Ein Sof, since the hardness of the screen rests upon the coarseness in phase four. Therefore we mostly mention only the screen alone in the matter of the drawing of the light, though the intention is necessarily upon both, as explained. And we too, in order to shorten the language, will call the drawing of the light from Ein Sof by the name of the screen alone, and likewise we will call the exiting of the degrees one from another by the name “the refinement of the coarseness,” though the intention is upon the hardness in the screen. And remember that the intention is upon the measures of coarseness in phase four which make the four phases of hardness in the screen.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:81
items.html:
The exit of the level of Hochma from phase three.
And the exit of the level of Hochma from the level of Keter was already explained well above, that the first ten Sefirot, which came out after the restriction, through the meeting of the upper light with the screen composed of the complete coarseness of phase four, as above (Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, item 64, Sub Header, “And therefore”), thus raised reflected light in the complete level up to the root, called Keter, and after that level was completed, in Rosh, Toch, and Sof, a portion of coarseness was refined from the screen, that is, from phase four to phase three, as above (Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, item 74). And since the screen acquired a disparity of form, it is considered to have exited outside the level of Keter, as above. And through the meeting of the light of Ein Sof with this screen that was refined to phase three, second Sefirot came out, whose level reaches only up to Hochma, and lacks Keter, as above (Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, item 78, Sub Header, “And the reason for the lack,” see there).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:82
items.html:
The exit of the level of Bina from phase two.
And after this level of Hochma was completed, in Rosh, Toch, and Sof, the surrounding light returned and refined another portion from the measure of coarseness of the screen, that is, from phase three of phase four to phase two of phase four, and this new screen of phase two of phase four is considered to have exited outside the level of Hochma, for the reason mentioned above regarding the level of Keter (see Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, item 76, Sub Header, “And already”). And from the meeting of the upper light with this new screen of phase two, new Sefirot came out at the level of Bina alone, and they lack Keter and Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:83
items.html:
The reason for the lack of Hochma in the screen of phase two.
And the reason for the lack of Hochma from this new level is the same reason given above (Histaklut Penimit, Part 2, items 75-76) for the lack of Keter, see there. Since this phase four has only the coarseness of phase two, which is regarded as the Bina of phase four, this drawing that it made was, from the outset, only from Bina downward. Therefore, even if the screen had not restrained the upper light, it likewise would not have expanded into phase four itself, but only from Bina downward. And it now follows that the screen did not return backward the Keter and Hochma that would have been fit for phase four; hence the Keter and Hochma are not found in this reflected light, and since the reflected light is not there, the upper light of Keter and Hochma is not there either, since they have no aspect of a vessel of reception.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:84
items.html:
The exit of the level of ZA from the screen of phase one.
And after this new level of the level of Bina was completed, in Rosh, Toch, and Sof, the surrounding light returned and refined yet another portion from the measure of coarseness in the screen, that is, from phase two to phase one, and this too is considered to have exited outside the level of Bina. And from the meeting of the upper light with the screen of phase one of phase four, new Sefirot came out at the level of Zeir Anpin. And here the first three Sefirot are lacking, namely Keter, Hochma, and Bina, for the reason mentioned above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 7:85
items.html:
The exit of the level of Malchut.
And after the level of Zeir Anpin was completed, in Rosh, Toch, and Sof, the last portion, of the coarseness of phase four, was also refined. And this too is considered, that this screen, once entirely refined, exited outside the level of Zeir Anpin, and it is called the level of Malchut, in which no new light whatsoever was renewed, but it receives illumination from Zeir Anpin, since it is no longer fit for drawing, as above; hence it has only the light of Nefesh, and the completion of this matter will be explained, God willing, in Part 3.
